newsitem.title: USA: Boeing elated by fighter jet announcement.
newsitem.headline: Boeing elated by fighter jet announcement.

text.p: Boeing Co. welcomed Saturday's announcement by the Pentagon that it will compete with Lockheed Martin Corp. in the final running for the manufacture of the next generation of fighter jets.
"I couldn't be happier," Boeing chief executive officer Phil Condit said at a news conference. "This is an absolutely great moment for us."

He said the Pentagon's decision was the culmination of a 20-year Boeing effort that has included several military contract victories including a major role in the F-22 fighter and a pact to build an airborne laser missile defense system.
"I don't want this to be a single-product company," Condit said. "I want it to be a diversified aerospace company that is good in a number of areas."

Lockheed Martin Corp. officials said they expect Boeing Co. to be a strong rival for the contract to build at least 3,000 joint strike fighters, a jet for use by several branches of the U.S. armed forces and the British Royal Navy.
The Pentagon said it was awarding Lockheed a $718.8 million contract and Boeing a $661.8 million contract to immediately begin work on their prototypes.
A third team led by McDonnell Douglas Corp. was eliminated from the running for the contract that could mean over $170 billion to the eventual winner.
While Boeing is the world's biggest builder of commercial jets, it has not built a fighter jet since World War II, and was considered the underdog in the competition by many.
